findings.title: queued default is evaluated once at module import, not per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated a single time when the class body is executed at import time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value (e.g. via `AssignmentSource.from_integration`) shares the same stale timestamp from when the process first imported the module. Dataclass defaults must be immutable values or use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. As written, the `queued` field is always wrong (it never reflects when the source was actually queued), which makes the field useless for debugging/tracing sync cycles — the very purpose of this dataclass. Fix: `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: from_dict does no type coercion; queued silently round-trips as a string through the Celery task
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` emits `queued` as a `datetime`, but the value is passed as a Celery task kwarg (`assignment_source_dict` in `sync_assignee_outbound`), where the JSON serializer converts it to an ISO-format string. `from_dict` then calls `cls(**input_dict)` with no validation or coercion, so the reconstructed `AssignmentSource.queued` is a `str`, not a `datetime`, despite the type annotation. Nothing consumes `queued` today so this is latent, but any future code that treats `queued` as a datetime (comparisons, arithmetic, `.isoformat()`) will fail only in the task (deserialized) path, not in tests that construct the dataclass directly. Either parse `queued` with `datetime.fromisoformat` in `from_dict`, drop the field, or store it as a string from the start.

findings.title: assignment_source added to abstract sync_status_outbound but never wired up
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` parameter, but no caller passes it (the `sync_status_outbound` Celery task is untouched) and no concrete implementation (Jira, Azure DevOps/VSTS, ExampleIntegration) accepts that parameter — several implement `sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` with no `**kwargs`, so any future caller passing the declared keyword would crash at runtime. This is dead, misleading API surface: it suggests status sync cycles are covered by this fix when only assignee sync is. Either remove the parameter from the abstract method or fully wire it through the status-sync path including the concrete implementations.
